PLAN YOUR REQUIREMENT

A useful brief.
A clearer next step.

New product development, drawing preparation, component redesign and reverse engineering.

Decisions to make early

Start with the function and interfaces: what must the part do, what must it fit, and which dimensions cannot change? Include assembly access, material preferences and the intended production quantity.

What to agree before work begins

Agree the required CAD format, drawing revision, dimensional information and review milestones before design work begins.

BEFORE YOU ENQUIRE

Questions,
answered.

Can I start with a sample or a sketch?+

A sketch, sample or existing drawing can be a starting point. Include the intended use, dimensions you know and the problem you want to solve. Measurement needs and the design scope are reviewed before work is agreed.

Which design files should I prepare?+

List the CAD and drawing formats you have, their revision and any files needed to understand the assembly. The required exchange format and final deliverables are agreed during the technical review.

A CLEAR START

What to share.

Your brief, reference files, intended use and key constraints.

Technical scope, material suitability, tolerances, inspection criteria, pricing and timing are confirmed after reviewing your requirements.

A CONNECTED APPROACH

Think beyond
one process.

Your project may need design, fabrication, finishing and assembly together. Include the complete requirement so each step can be considered in context.
